verses.text: Foolish Galatians! Who has put a spell on you? Jesus Christ was clearly shown to you as crucified.
I just want to ask you one thing. Did you receive the Spirit by keeping the law, or by hearing and believing?
Are you so foolish? You began with the Spirit. Are you now trying to finish by your own human effort?
Did you suffer so much for nothing? Surely it was not for nothing!
God gives you his Spirit and does miracles among you. Does he do it because you keep the law, or because you hear and believe?
It is just like Abraham. "He believed God, and God counted it to him as being right with him."
So you can see that those who have faith are the children of Abraham.
The Scriptures saw ahead that God would make the Gentiles right with him by faith. So they told the Good News to Abraham beforehand: "All nations will be blessed through you."
So those who have faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
All who depend on keeping the law are under a curse. It is written, "Cursed is everyone who does not keep on doing everything written in the book of the law."
It is clear that no one is made right with God by the law, because "The righteous will live by faith."
The law is not based on faith. Instead, it says, "The person who does these things will live by them."
Christ set us free from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. It is written, "Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree."
He did this so that the blessing given to Abraham would come to the Gentiles through Christ Jesus. Then by faith we could receive the Spirit God promised.
Brothers and sisters, let me give an example from everyday life. When a person's agreement has been made firm, no one can cancel it or add to it.
God made his promises to Abraham and to his offspring. It does not say "to offsprings", meaning many people. It says "to your offspring", meaning one person, who is Christ.
This is what I mean. God first made a firm agreement. The law came four hundred and thirty years later. It cannot cancel the agreement and so do away with the promise.
If the inheritance comes from the law, then it no longer comes from the promise. But God gave it freely to Abraham through a promise.
Then why was the law given? It was added because of wrongdoing, until the offspring came to whom the promise was made. It was put in place through angels, by a go-between.
A go-between is needed when there is more than one side. But God is one.
So is the law against God's promises? Certainly not! If a law had been given that could give life, then we could be made right with God by the law.
But the Scriptures show that the whole world is held prisoner by sin. So the promise is given through faith in Jesus Christ to those who believe.
Before this faith came, we were held under the law like prisoners. We were locked up until the faith that was coming would be shown.
So the law was our guardian to lead us to Christ, so that we could be made right with God by faith.
But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a guardian.
You are all children of God through faith in Christ Jesus.
All of you who were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
There is no Jew or Greek, no slave or free person, no male or female. You are all one in Christ Jesus.
If you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's offspring. You will receive what God promised.
